# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

## Headline finding: the whole val set is blocked by a host-side infra bug, not a capability gap
Diagnosing ALL 50 trajectories (not just the 8 "controllable" ones) shows a single shared
root cause: every task fails with a `PermissionError` on the `/mnt/data` mount.
- `/mnt/data` is `drwx------ (0o40700) uid=1004`, but the code kernel runs as `uid=1000 (jovyan), gid=100(users)`.
- The container can neither READ the input (`/mnt/data/spreadsheet/<id>/...`) nor WRITE the
  output (`/mnt/data/outputs/<tag>/...`). `namei -l` shows "Permission denied" at the `data` node.
- Captured error on 42/50: `"sandbox denied writes to the bind-mounted output dir ... the host dir
  is not writable by the container's uid; see _make_container_writable"`. The other 8 hit the same
  wall but with no captured `error` field (hence the framework's spurious "8 controllable" label).
- Agents already tried every reachable workaround across traces: `chmod`, `chown`, `sudo`,
  `os.access`, `/tmp`, `setuid`, `namei`, `find` — all denied. 30 rounds burned per task.

`_make_container_writable` is a RUNNER-side helper; it did not run / failed. This is an
infrastructure bug outside the editable artifact (system prompt) and outside any
agent-reachable action. No prompt text can make a 0700 host dir owned by another uid accessible.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag (KNOWLEDGE / BEHAVIORAL / CAPABILITY-GAP) | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | host bind-mount not writable/readable by container uid | ALL 50 | `/mnt/data` 0700 uid=1004 vs kernel uid=1000; `_make_container_writable` failed | INFRA (uncontrollable) | none possible from prompt — reported to run owner |
| 2 | agent burns all 30 rounds probing the sandbox instead of committing its already-correct solution | all 50 (behavioral; only matters in a healthy env) | prompt doesn't tell agent a PermissionError on the FIXED paths is environmental, not a code bug to debug | BEHAVIORAL / KNOWLEDGE | additive prompt rule (below) |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit — aim for MULTIPLE classes, incl. a NEW tool when a cluster needs one)
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | Add missing rule (KNOWLEDGE) + positive-framing anti-stall | prompt.md | Distinguish a CODE error (fix & retry) from an ENVIRONMENT error on the fixed input/output paths (PermissionError / read-only mount / bind-mount write-denied) which the code cannot fix; in that case emit ONE complete solution to output_path and stop rather than probing id/namei/chmod/sudo for rounds. Also: don't narrate a plan across rounds without executing; emit one self-contained final code block. | Yes — see blast radius |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change: the trace it targets → what it now does on those exact inputs)
- Env-error rule: in the 30709 trace the agent hit `PermissionError` on input at msg 3 then spent
  msgs 4–61 probing id/namei/find/chmod/sudo/setuid and re-emitting the (already-correct) solution
  ~10×. The new rule tells it to classify that as environmental and commit once — the ONLY
  prompt-addressable behavior in the traces. Blast radius: in a HEALTHY environment no
  PermissionError is raised, so the environment-error branch NEVER triggers → zero behavior change on
  any task that would pass; the seed's first solution code (30709 msg 4) is already correct and would
  write output on round 1. BOUNDED. It cannot regress a correct solution and cannot loosen any
  decision rule (purely additive, error-branch only).

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees / parallel features used (or: "serial fallback because …"): Serial diagnosis;
  parsed all 50 trajectory JSONs programmatically to confirm the error is universal and identical
  (42 host write-denied errors + 8 same permission wall). No worktrees needed — one prompt edit.
- Prior iterations I read from ./prior_iterations/ + ./RUNMAP.md: none exist — this is the seed
  (LEDGER/RUNMAP/JOURNAL have no prior results).

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- The seed prompt's core spreadsheet guidance is already correct (openpyxl over pandas, literal
  values over formulas, respect answer_position range, save to exact output_path). Do NOT churn it —
  the failures are NOT caused by it. The seed's solution CODE was correct on the tasks inspected.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why — already-passing / needs gold / infra noise)
- Cluster 1 (the host mount permission bug): UNCONTROLLABLE from the system prompt. Fixing it
  requires the runner to make the bind-mounted `/mnt/data` (and per-task output subdirs) owned by /
  writable by the container uid (`_make_container_writable`). Reported to the run owner; no prompt
  edit attempted (would fail the REAL + VERIFIED tests — reward stays 0.000 regardless).
- No speculative spreadsheet-correctness prompt rules added: no correctness cluster exists in the
  traces (every failure is the permission wall), so any such edit would target a hypothetical and
  fail test #1 (REAL).
